title.narrative: Shaml - Protection and Reintegration of Furthest-left-behind (UN Women Pilot)
Shaml - Protection and Reintegration of Furthest-left-behind (UN Women Pilot)

description.narrative:
Det föreslagna projektet, Enhancing the Protection and Reintegration of Furthest Left Behind Groups of Women and Girls Victims and Survivors of Violence in Palestine (2020-2022) ska genomföras av UN Women i Palestina.
Programmet är väl i linje med stödområde 1 i den nya strategin för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete med Palestina 2020-2024 "Mänskliga Rättigheter, demokrati, rättsstatens principer och jämställdhet", med huvudsyfte att åtgärda brister i policyer och tjänster för återintegrering och skydd. Det är ett pilotprojekt då det länkar samman tre områden inom samma stödområde: mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet och hälsa, vilket är ett relativt nytt sätt att arbeta inom ramen för strategin.

The proposed project, Enhancing the Protection and Reintegration of Furthest Left Behind Groups of Women and Girls Victims and Survivors of Violence in Palestine (2020-2022), is to be implemented by UN Women Palestine.
The project aligns with support area 1 of the new strategy for Sweden's international development cooperation with Palestine 2020-2024, 'Strengthened democracy, improved gender equality and greater respect for human rights', with the main objective of addressing the gaps in protection and reintegration policies and services. It is a pilot project in the sense that it interlinks the three areas under that support area: human rights, gender, and health, which is a relatively new approach within the strategy.

Impact: Furthest left behind women and girls in Palestine live a life free of violence. Outcome 1: Policy/decision makers' attitudes are more favorable towards the rights of furthest left behind groups of women and girls, survivors and victims of violence. Output 1.1: Knowledge and perception of policy/decision makers are enhanced and sensitized towards the rights of the furthest left behind groups of women and girls, victims and survivors of violence. Output 1.2: Women and human rights organizations are more capable to advocate for the rights of furthest left behind groups of women and girls, victims and survivors of violence. Outcome 2: Furthest left behind groups of women and girls access to quality and inclusive protection and reintegration services is enhanced. Output 2.1: Service providers develop and provide quality, accessible and more inclusive protection and reintegration services to the three identified groups of the furthest left behind groups of i) women and girls victims and survivors of violence (Girls in conflict with the law and victims and survivors of violence),ii) elderly women with disabilities, and iii) women and girls drug addicts. Output 2.2: Furthest left behind groups of women and girls (and their families) are more aware of their rights and the available services and how to use them. Output 2.3: Communities are supported to promote and uphold human rights of the furthest left behind groups of women and girls, survivors and victims of violence.

title.narrative: Decision on contribution regarding "Shaml - Protection and Reintegration of Furthest-left-behind (Pilot Program with UN Women)"

description.narrative:
Among main achievement in 2022 are:
- The Ministry of Social Development (MoSD) took a progressive decision towards the rights of the furthest left behind groups (FLBGs) of women and girls for protection and access to sheltering services. Despite the fact that the Cabinets decision of 2011 which denies the right of seven groups of women survivors of violence for sheltering services is still applicable, the Minister submitted an official letter to the Council of Ministers informing them about the Ministrys plan to rehabilitate an emergency shelter in Beitunia to provide protection services to women users of drugs, women sex workers and women with disabilities.
- MoSD through cooperation with UN Women Shaml programme have agreed to develop a functional plan to guide the development of the vision, mission, objectives, and scope of the Centre, including types of cases, scope and types of services, admission policies, safety and security considerations, capacity of the Centre, coordination and referral mechanisms, and required human resources amongst others, and a Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs).
- MoSD took a decision to review and amend the Cabinets decision of 2011 to ensure the right for all groups of women for protection and sheltering services.
- Ministry of Womens Affairs (MoWA) through collaboration with Shaml programme and other actors developed the new National Strategy to Combat Violence Against Women (2023-2029).
- 81 decision makers (50 women, 31 men) from the West Bank and Gaza representing governmental and non-governmental organizations have raised their awareness and sensitivity towards the rights of the FLBGs of women and girls victims and survivors of violence through their participation in review sessions and in the 16 days of activism related interventions.
- Seven new services have been adapted or piloted to meet the needs of the FLBGs of women and girls survivors of violence, including the Emergency Shelter in Beitunia; the Elderly Centre in Jericho, the Girls Care Centre in Beit Jala; 3 safe spaces for women survivors of violence in three targeted locations were made available, including at Ibda Association - Al Dheisheh Refugee Camp, YWCA - Jalazoun- Jalazoun Refugee Camp, and Al Finique Association - Al Aroub Refugee Camp; and finally the EGG system to provide medical services to women users of drugs in Gaza was made available.
- In 2022, a total of 13,889 persons (7,885 females, 6,004 males) from the West Bank and Gaza, including women and girls of the FLBGs, families members of women and girls of the FLBGs, decision makers, women and men have raised their awareness and knowledge about the rights of the FLBGs of women and girls victims and survivors of violence and the available services.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
